units.text: INT. MINICAB - MOVING - 2 A.M.
A tired Toyota Prius, smelling of pine air freshener and last Friday.
Rain on the Westway.
The driver, BARRY QUILL, 50s, cardigan, thermos in the cup holder, has the radio on low, playing something regrettable from 1987.
In the back, THE WOMAN, 30s, immaculate in a camel coat that has never seen a bus, looks out of the window and says nothing.
Beside her sits a violin case, which Barry noticed and chose not to mention.
ON PHONE (her screen): "Two minutes out.
Bring the case.
Don't be clever."
Dreadful night for it.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: For what?
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: Whatever you're doing. Orchestra, is it?
units.name: BARRY

units.text: Something like that.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: Her phone shows a second message: "Gate B. Quartet's in position."
Barry drives on, serene as a vicar.
I did a gig once. Trombone. Fell off the stage at a Rotary dinner. Terribly embarrassing.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: I'm sure you recovered.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: They turn into the gates of the Hatton Auction House, shuttered and dark.
Four figures in black coats wait beneath the awning: THE QUARTET, holding what are almost certainly instruments.
Evening, Mrs Vance.
units.name: THE QUARTET

units.text: Keep it, Mr Quill.
units.name: THE WOMAN
paren: to Barry, handing over a fifty

units.text: I don't recall telling you my surname.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: She opens the violin case.
It is empty, lined in velvet, exactly the size of a small painting.
Ah.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: Wait here, would you? There's a good chap.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: She leaves.
Barry looks at the thermos, at the rain, at the radio.
Then, quite calmly, he turns the engine off.
